questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend checking for an existing base Lightning component before building custom UI from raw HTML?
options: Base components are the only elements allowed inside an LWC template
Base components already handle SLDS styling and accessibility concerns like ARIA attributes and keyboard interaction, work you'd otherwise have to redo yourself
Raw HTML elements cannot be used inside LWC templates at all
Base components are required for a component to be exposed in Lightning App Builder
questions.explain: Base components ship already styled with SLDS and already handle accessibility concerns -- building the same UI from raw HTML means redoing that styling and accessibility work yourself.

questions.q: How does `lightning-input` cover many different form field types without needing a separate component per type?
options: It requires a separate wrapper component for each field type
Through its `type` attribute, which can be set to values like text, email, search, checkbox, date, or number
It only supports plain text input and nothing else
By inheriting from lightning-textarea automatically
questions.explain: A single lightning-input component covers many field types via its type attribute, rather than requiring a distinct base component for each possible kind of input.

questions.q: In the lightning-card example, how is the 'New Case' button placed into the card's action area?
options: By setting an @api property named actionButton on lightning-card
By placing the button inside the card's markup with slot="actions"
By calling a JavaScript method named addAction() on the card
lightning-card does not support any action buttons
questions.explain: lightning-card exposes a named 'actions' slot -- content placed inside the card's tags with slot="actions" renders in that designated action area, directly applying the slot pattern from Lesson 13.

questions.q: Which base component is used for structured tabular data with built-in sorting, inline editing, and row-selection support?
options: lightning-accordion
lightning-tree
lightning-datatable
lightning-tabset
questions.explain: lightning-datatable is the Tables and Trees category component built specifically for structured tabular data, with sorting, inline editing on editable columns, and row selection already built in.

questions.q: Which category does `lightning-accordion` and `lightning-tabset` belong to, per this lesson's grouping?
options: Input
Actions and Menus
Containers
Notifications
questions.explain: lightning-accordion and lightning-tabset are Containers components, used for structuring a page's layout -- distinct from Input (form fields), Actions and Menus (buttons/menus), and Notifications (spinners, toasts).
